newsitem.title: TURKEY: Key Turkish security council meeting begins.
newsitem.headline: Key Turkish security council meeting begins.

text.p: Turkey's National Security Council, grouping senior ministers and the top armed forces commanders, met on Saturday to press the secularist military's demands for a crackdown on Islamist activities.
The influential council, dominated by the top brass, began its regular monthly session at 3 p.m.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and armed forces chief Ismail Hakki Karadayi sat in the meeting room with large folders on a table in front of them before the session started.

No agenda has been made public but senior officers said the meeting would review evidence of what they see as the unacceptable spread of Islamic activity, fostered by Erbakan and his Islam-based Welfare Party.
The growing row over the role of Islam in the public life of officially secular Turkey has threatened to split the junior partner conservatives from Erbakan's Islamist wing.
Two conservative ministers resigned on Saturday in protest at the government's reluctance to implement an anti-Islamist programme demanded two months ago by the NSC.

Top of the generals' list of 18 anti-Islamist demands is a call for educational reform that would require students to attend eight years of secular schooling -- rather than the current five years -- before electing optional Koranic training.
Other elements include enforcement of existing bans on traditional Islamic dress, limits on anti-secularist media and restrictions on the secretive Moslem orders.
